==English== ===Etymology=== [[File:Back on the road.jpg|thumb|Preparing to '''pull''' a car from the mud with a rope ({{senseno|en|apply force}})]] Verb from {{inh|en|enm|pullen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|pullian|t=to pull, draw, tug, pluck off}}, of uncertain ultimate origin. Related to {{cog|fy|pûlje|t=to shell, husk}}, {{cog|dum|pullen|t=to drink}}, {{cog|dum|polen|t=to peel, strip}}, {{cog|nds|pulen|t=to pick, pluck, pull, tear, strip off husks}}, {{cog|is|púla|t=to work hard, beat}}. Noun from {{inh|en|enm|pul}}, {{m|enm|pull}}, {{m|enm|pulle}}, from the verb {{m|enm|pullen|t=to pull}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|po͝ol|a=RP,GA}}; {{IPA|en|/pʊl/}} * {{audio|en|En-us-pull.ogg|a=GA}} * {{IPA|en|/pəl/|a=Central England,Southern England,RP}} * {{IPA|en|/pʉl/|a=Scotland,Northern Ireland}} * {{IPA|en|/puːl/|a=full-fool}} * {{audio|en|En-au-pull.ogg|a=AU}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q7976 (mis)-Le Rêveur0316-pull.wav|a=Western Pennsylvania}} * {{homophones|en|pool> or <>>}} * {{rhymes|en|ʊl|s=1}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{senseid|en|apply force}} {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To apply a [[force]] to (an object) so that it comes [[toward]] the person or thing applying the force. #: {{ux|en|When I give the signal, '''pull''' the rope.}} #: {{ux|en|Pull your belt tight before [[starting off]], will you?}} #: {{ux|en|I '''pulled''' the door to after me.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Genesis|8|9|passage=He put forth his hand {{...}} and '''pulled''' her in.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Macbeth|IV|iii|passage=Ne'er '''pull''' your hat upon your brows.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Searching for the Secrets of Gravity|author=John Boslough|page=574 |text=All the gravitational mass of the earth '''pulls''' toward a single point at the planet's center, overwhelming the miniscule pull of other objects.}} # To [[gather#Verb|gather]] with the hand, or by drawing toward oneself; to [[pluck#Verb|pluck]] or [[pick#Verb|pick]] (flowers, fruit, etc.). #: {{ux|en|to '''pull''' fruit from a tree}} #: {{ux|en|'''pull''' flax}} #: {{ux|en|'''pull''' a finch}} #* {{RQ:Smollett Peregrine Pickle|volume=I|19|text=He and some of his companions one day entered a garden in the suburbs, and having indulged their appetites, desired to know what satisfaction they must make for the fruit they had '''pulled'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[attract]] or [[net#Verb|net]]; to [[pull in]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Marcella Ridlen Ray|title=Changing and Unchanging Face of United States Civil Society |passage=Television, a favored source of news and information, '''pulls''' the largest share of advertising monies.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|author=Russell Simmons; Chris Morrow|title=Super Rich: A Guide to Having It All |passage=While the pimp can always '''pull''' a ho with his magnetism, he can never '''pull''' a nun. The nun is too in touch with her own compassionate and honest spirit to react to a spirit as negative and deceitful as that of the pimp.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive|chiefly|UK|Ireland|slang}} To persuade (someone) to [[have sex]] with one. #: {{ux|en|I '''pulled''' at the club last night.}} #: {{ux|en|He's '''pulled''' that bird over there.}} #: {{ux|en|Grab your coat, love, you've '''pulled'''.}} # {{lb|en|ambitransitive|US|slang}} To interest (someone) in dating or pursuing one (whether or not this has led to sex). # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[remove]] or [[withdraw]] (something), especially from public [[circulation]] or [[availability]]. #: {{ux|en|Each day, they '''pulled''' the old bread and set out fresh loaves.}} #: {{ux|en|The book was due to be released today, but it was '''pulled''' at the last minute over legal concerns.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[retrieve]] or [[look up]] for use. #: {{ux|en|I'll have to '''pull''' a part number for that.}} #: {{ux|en|This computer file is incorrect. Can we '''pull''' the old version from your backups?}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Michael Bellomo; Joel Elad|title=How to Sell Anything on Amazon...and Make a Fortune! |passage=They'll go through their computer system and '''pull''' a report of all your order fulfillment records for the time period you specify.}} # {{lb|en|construction}} To obtain (a [[permit#Noun|permit]]) from a regulatory authority. #: {{ux|en|It's the contractor's responsibility to '''pull''' the necessary permits before starting work.}} # {{senseid|en|do something bad}} {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To [[do#Verb|do]] or [[perform]], especially something seen as negative by the speaker. #: {{ux|en|He regularly '''pulls''' 12-hour days, sometimes 14.}} #: {{ux|en|You'll be sent home if you '''pull''' another stunt like that.}} #: {{ux|en|What are you trying to '''pull'''?}} #* {{RQ:EarthBound|What are you trying to '''pull''', anyway?
